diet.description: Capitalised, because that is how canon writes it. Sparse -- 40 of 347 -- and not required.

journal_prompt.description: Player-facing prose read in the travel journal. Distinct from `notes`: `notes` is a reference fact for the canon reader, `journal_prompt` is the sentence the player sees. Exported as `journalPrompt`.

region.description: Bestiary region of origin, kept for provenance.

biomes.description: Where this species lives, from the canonical vocabulary in database/biomes.json. Wider than the game's biome set on purpose: canon can say 'floating island' or 'Naraka rifts' even though the walk has nowhere to put them. The export keeps only the renderable ones, and a species left with none becomes placement 'lore' automatically. An empty list means nobody has tagged this yet -- say where it lives instead.

placement.description: Whether the species can be met (`encounter`), only mentioned in passing (`flavour`), or exists in the record alone (`lore`).

rarity.description: How often a player meets one. Drives the weighting the game expands biome pools with, so a fourth value silently changes encounter rates.

sentient.description: Taxonomic marker for the avian-dinosaurid and other sapient lineages (Cognitavi, Nagaraptor, Vajraptor, Silvanus, Sylvians, Kuktush). It records that a species is intelligent and socially organised -- see AI_CONTEXT.md:998-1006 -- and nothing more. It is NOT a placement rule: in-world the Harappans regard these as animals, so a sentient species sitting in the encounter table is correct, not an oversight.

epochs.description: Epoch ids from database/timeline/epochs.json. Absent means present in all epochs.

source_index.description: Position in the authored bestiary sequence (prototype starters first for fauna). Array order decides which species pickFor lands on for a tile, so this is part of the seed contract, not presentation.

placement_note.description: Why this species is placed as it is, when the answer is not obvious. Required reading before 'fixing' an entity with empty `biomes`: an empty list can mean untagged, or it can mean deliberately held out of play. If this field is present, the emptiness is a decision.

crosses_at.description: Entity ids of the places where a species native to another realm enters this one. Naraka creatures cross at the Dwarka Gate (settlement_dwarka) rather than being native to delta water, so they should be met near a gate and nowhere else.

aliases.description: Other names this creature is known by. Two fauna carry one, and neither schema nor linter knew until `additionalProperties` was tightened.
